# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by `synthigy __docs`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Run a Synthigy instance, or connect your code to one

## Client — connect developers, services and bots to a Synthigy server

### `synthigy connect`

Authenticate against a Synthigy server and save the connection to this profile

```
synthigy connect <server-url> [flags]
```

Examples:

```
  synthigy connect http://localhost:7887
  synthigy connect https://server.example.com --insecure
  synthigy connect https://server.example.com --client-id svc --client-secret "$SECRET"
  synthigy --env .synthigy/customer2.env connect https://customer2.example.com
```

Flags:

```
      --client-id string       Connect as a service: this client's id (non-interactive)
      --client-secret string   Connect as a service: this client's secret (or set SYNTHIGY_CLIENT_SECRET)
      --insecure               Skip TLS certificate verification
      --user                   Force the device-flow (browser) login, skipping the interactive prompt
  -v, --verbose                Verbose output
```

### `synthigy disconnect`

Disconnect from server and revoke tokens

```
synthigy disconnect
```

Examples:

```
  synthigy disconnect
  synthigy --env .synthigy/customer2.env disconnect
```

### `synthigy exec`

Run a command under an instance's env (discovered, or explicit -f profiles)

```
synthigy exec [-f FILE...] -- COMMAND [ARGS...] [flags]
```

Flags:

```
  -f, --env-file stringArray   env file to load instead of discovery (repeatable; later files win)
      --show                   print the merged keys to stderr before running (secrets masked)
```

### `synthigy schema`

The schema snapshot XSQL editor tooling reads

```
synthigy schema
```

#### `synthigy schema check`

Fail when <dir>/schema.json is older than the deployed model

```
synthigy schema check [flags]
```

Examples:

```
  synthigy schema check
  synthigy schema check --dir queries
```

Flags:

```
      --dir string   Directory holding .xsql sources and schema.json (default "xsql")
```

#### `synthigy schema pull`

Refresh <dir>/schema.json from the connected instance

```
synthigy schema pull [flags]
```

Examples:

```
  synthigy schema pull
  synthigy schema pull --dir queries
  synthigy schema pull --role Editor --role Viewer
  synthigy --env .synthigy/customer2.env schema pull
```

Flags:

```
      --dir string         Directory holding .xsql sources; schema.json is written here (default "xsql")
      --role stringArray   project the schema onto this role (repeatable)
```

### `synthigy token`

Print a fresh access token for this profile's saved identity

```
synthigy token
```

Examples:

```
  synthigy token
  synthigy --env .synthigy/customer2.env token
```

### `synthigy whoami`

Show current user information

```
synthigy whoami
```

Examples:

```
  synthigy whoami
  synthigy --env .synthigy/customer2.env whoami
```

## Server — run and operate a Synthigy instance here

### `synthigy clean`

Prune cached releases and old JREs from ~/.synthigy

```
synthigy clean [flags]
```

Flags:

```
      --keep int   Number of most recent releases to keep (default 2)
```

### `synthigy console`

Open the portal: setup, health and configuration of the instance on this machine

```
synthigy console [flags]
```

Flags:

```
  -p, --print   Print the URL only, don't open a browser
```

### `synthigy down`

Stop the engine and the portal started by 'up'

```
synthigy down
```

### `synthigy iam`

Export, import and script IAM configuration

```
synthigy iam
```

#### `synthigy iam add-client`

Create an OAuth client (and its service user), scripted

```
synthigy iam add-client <name> [flags]
```

Flags:

```
      --api stringArray        audience this client may request a token for (repeatable, confidential only)
      --grant stringArray      allowed grant type, e.g. client_credentials (repeatable)
      --id string              client id (default: server-generated)
      --local                  go through the portal of the instance on this machine instead of a connected server
      --redirect stringArray   allowed redirect URI for authorization_code (repeatable)
      --role stringArray       grant this role to the service user (repeatable, confidential only)
      --secret string          pin the client secret instead of generating one; on an existing client this is the only way to change it
      --trusted                mark the client trusted: no consent screen, and it may run requests as its users (acting_as)
      --type string            public or confidential (default "public")
```

#### `synthigy iam export`

Export IAM configuration as JSON to stdout

```
synthigy iam export <type> [name...] [flags]
```

Flags:

```
      --id stringArray   export only the record with this id (repeatable; only OAuth clients have one)
```

#### `synthigy iam import`

Import IAM configuration from a JSON file

```
synthigy iam import <type> <file> [flags]
```

Flags:

```
      --dry-run       validate without writing
      --mode string   sync (declarative) or stack (additive) (default "sync")
```

#### `synthigy iam remove-client`

Delete an OAuth client and its service user

```
synthigy iam remove-client <id>
```

### `synthigy logs`

Show this instance's engine process log (boot and crash output)

```
synthigy logs [flags]
```

Examples:

```
  synthigy logs
  synthigy logs -f
  synthigy logs -n 500
```

Flags:

```
  -f, --follow      Keep printing as the log grows
  -n, --lines int   Number of trailing lines to print (default 200)
```

### `synthigy pull`

Download a release's bundle into the cache without starting anything

```
synthigy pull [flags]
```

Examples:

```
  synthigy pull --bundle postgres
  synthigy pull --bundle sqlite --version v0.2.12
```

Flags:

```
      --bundle string    Bundle: sqlite | postgres | postgres-clickhouse (default "sqlite")
      --version string   Release version (e.g. v0.2.12) (default "latest")
```

### `synthigy service`

Run this instance as a boot-time service (systemd user unit / launchd agent)

```
synthigy service
```

#### `synthigy service install`

Install and enable the service for the current instance home

```
synthigy service install
```

#### `synthigy service status`

Show the service's state

```
synthigy service status
```

#### `synthigy service uninstall`

Stop, disable and remove the service (the instance data is untouched)

```
synthigy service uninstall
```

### `synthigy up`

Start the Synthigy engine (cold start: provisions JRE, launches the JVM)

```
synthigy up [flags]
```

Examples:

```
  synthigy up                                # opens the setup wizard on a fresh install
  synthigy up --bundle postgres              # needs POSTGRES_* env; persists the choice
  synthigy up --version v0.2.12              # pin a release
  synthigy up --jar synthigy.jar             # local/airgap jar, no download
  synthigy up --join                         # stay attached (systemd / launchd / container PID 1)
  synthigy --env .synthigy/customer1.env up  # replaces <instance-home>/.env, for running several instances
```

Flags:

```
      --bundle string    Bundle: sqlite | postgres | postgres-clickhouse — write-through to .env; missing and unset opens the wizard
      --force            Re-download every module even if cached (suspected corruption)
      --jar string       Local jar, or a classpath of module jars, instead of a release download; airgap/custom builds
      --join             Stay attached to this terminal instead of detaching — for process supervisors (systemd Type=simple, launchd, a container's PID 1), which need the process they started to keep running
      --version string   Release version to run (e.g. v0.2.12) (default "latest")
```

### `synthigy versions`

List available Synthigy releases

```
synthigy versions
```

## Common

### `synthigy completion`

Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell

```
synthigy completion
```

### `synthigy doctor`

Run system health checks

```
synthigy doctor
```

### `synthigy env`

Manage this project's local Synthigy instance (.synthigy/.env)

```
synthigy env
```

#### `synthigy env init`

Scaffold ./.synthigy for a project-local instance

```
synthigy env init
```

### `synthigy status`

Show this instance and its saved connection, offline

```
synthigy status
```

Examples:

```
  synthigy status
  synthigy --env .synthigy/customer2.env status
```

### `synthigy upgrade`

Upgrade (or downgrade) the synthigy CLI binary

```
synthigy upgrade [flags]
```

Examples:

```
  synthigy upgrade
  synthigy upgrade --version v0.1.9   # pin an older CLI
```

Flags:

```
      --version string   CLI release tag to install (e.g. v0.1.10) (default "latest")
```

### `synthigy version`

Print version information

```
synthigy version
```

## Global flags

```
      --env string   Profile file to use instead of <instance-home>/.env (default: $SYNTHIGY_ENV_FILE)
  -v, --verbose      Verbose output
```
